dossier.public_summary: The dip repeats exactly as the star spins every 1.03 days and gets much weaker when the star is viewed at different spot phases, with a deep spot modulation larger than the dip itself. That pattern is produced by rotating starspots on a highly variable M dwarf, not by a planet crossing the star.

reasons.why: Signal period is essentially identical to the star's spot period in every sector, with huge rotation amplitude (22439 ppm in sector 15) far exceeding the 2990 ppm dip. Variable temperature blocking from the same spots produces the dip, not a planet.

Large coherent swing at the same period outside transit (ratio 1.2 of depth) and sector-to-sector depth collapse (5155 ppm in sector 15 to -26 ppm in sector 49) are classic spot-modulation signatures; planet transits do not vanish while the spot signal remains.

reasons.why: Huge Gaia astrometric excess and density mismatch show the light is dominated by a very variable spotted dwarf, not a quiet host. Combined with low xgboost planet_rank 0.08, the best explanation is stellar variability / blended variability on the target, not a quiet planet transit.
